W-BUDGET.v1: RabbitMQ {{version}} counts every return of a quorum-queue message against its delivery limit ({{limit}}). Peeking uses 1 of each message's {{limit}} delivery attempts. Messages that have already used {{limit}} will be {{disposition}} by this peek.

W-313.v1: On RabbitMQ 3.13 every peek increases x-delivery-count. Delivery limit: {{limit}}. Where a limit is set, messages already at it are dead-lettered or deleted by this peek.

W-TAIL.v1: This quorum queue has no delivery limit, so RabbitMQ {{version}} puts returned messages at the back: peeking moves these {{count}} messages behind {{behind}} others.

W-OVERLIMIT.v1: This queue receives dead-lettered messages from {{sources}}. Its delivery limit ({{limit}}) is not higher than theirs, so messages that died for exceeding a delivery limit arrive with a count above {{limit}}. RabbitMQ {{consequence}} such messages on ANY return, including this peek. Set delivery-limit to -1 (or at least {{minimum}}) on this queue first.

W-DELAY.v1: Delayed retry is on ({{type}}, min {{min}} ms, max {{max}} ms). Messages returned by this peek are held back for at least {{min}} ms; consumers will not receive them during that time.

W-REDELIVERED.v1: Peeked messages will reach their next consumer with redelivered=true{{counterNote}}.

W-HOLD.v1: For up to {{seconds}} s these messages are unavailable to consumers, which may process later messages first.

W-DROPHEAD.v1: This queue is near its length limit ({{ready}}/{{max}}, overflow=drop-head). While the peek holds messages they don't count toward the limit; if publishers fill the gap, RabbitMQ will {{action}} the oldest messages when the peek returns them, starting with the peeked ones.

W-TTL.v1: Messages expire after {{ttl}}. Any message whose TTL passes during the peek will be {{fate}} when it is returned.

W-CRASH.v1: If this tool's connection breaks before the messages are returned, RabbitMQ counts it as a failed delivery (x-delivery-count +1) for every held message.

W-SAC-CQ.v1: Single active consumer is on. basic.get bypasses it: the active consumer may process later messages before the peeked ones are returned, breaking strict ordering.

W-SAC-QQ.v1: RabbitMQ refuses basic.get on quorum queues with single active consumer. Peeking registers a consumer that will be the active one while it runs; real consumers wait until it ends.

W-EXCLUSIVE.v1: This exclusive queue belongs to another connection; RabbitMQ does not allow reading it.

W-UPGRADED.v1: RabbitMQ reports delivery limit '{{stat}}' for this queue, but its arguments and policies imply {{computed}}. The queue was probably created before 4.0, and any policy change that matches it will apply {{computed}}.

W-MIXED.v1: Cluster nodes run different versions ({{list}}); quorum queues keep the older rules until every node is upgraded. Using {{era}} rules.

W-STREAM.v1: Reading a stream with an anonymous reader does not remove or change messages. A named consumer would store its offset.
